title: Extractive Summarization of Long Documents by Combining Global and Local Context
answer_short: Local context refers to the section/topic within a document, while global context refers to the whole document.
answer_rationale: The document explicitly defines local context as the section/topic within a document and global context as the whole document, particularly in the context of summarization. This is stated in Text 2, section 10, where the authors propose to capture a distributed representation of both the global (the whole document) and the local context (e.g., the section/topic) when deciding if a sentence should be included in the summary.
